request: 每次任务完成归档后，对当前未归档的队伍的所有成员压缩上下文

trigger.meaning: When EVERY task of a team has reached a terminal state, fire ONE compaction pass for that team.
rejected: any single task reaching a terminal state
the team being archived via agent_teams_delete
trigger.note: This is the lower-frequency reading: one pass per completed team, not one per task.

who.choice: 等所有成员都空闲再一起压
who.meaning: A barrier: wait until every member of that team is idle, then compact them together.
who.why: ctx.compaction.compactNow requires an idle agent - ManualCompactAgentContext.runMaintenance throws synchronously when the agent is already active, and the expected-failure code is 'busy'.

teamScope.choice: 所有未归档队伍的全部成员
teamScope.meaning: Iterate every non-archived team record; compact the members of each.

threshold.meaning: Call compactNow on every pass, not compactIfNeeded. A pass with no safely compactable range legitimately returns null and is recorded as such.

safety.choice: 写审计记录 + 失败码逐条归档
safety.meaning: Every pass writes an audit record: team, member, session, whether it was skipped as busy, shadowedSeqCount / shadowedTokenCount, summarySeq, and the failure code when one occurs. Nothing silent.

placement.why: Does not touch the adopted upstream agent-teams code, so it avoids both the single-writer zone and the region-registry machinery.
placement.consequence: It must discover task-terminal transitions and member-to-agent mapping on its own; those are the open feasibility questions.

harnessFacts.composition: presets/mpd/agent.cordis.yml:264-289 already composes the compaction plane: the `compaction` service plus compaction-basic, command-compact and compaction-tool-result-pruner. So ctx.compaction is live in an mpd session and in member sessions.
harnessFacts.api: CompactionEngine.compactNow(agent: ManualCompactAgentContext, signal, sourceCommandId?) => CompactionResult | null
harnessFacts.agentRequirement: ManualCompactAgentContext = { session, options } + runMaintenance(task); runMaintenance THROWS SYNCHRONOUSLY when the agent is already active.
harnessFacts.irreversibility: A successful compaction REPLACES the selected history span with one summary node. Details are lost; this is why the audit record is a user requirement, not a nicety.
harnessFacts.existingHumanPath: dsh-command-compact registers the /compact command and calls ctx.compaction.compactNow(invocation.agent, invocation.signal, invocation.commandId) - the same API this feature will drive programmatically.

userDecisionsFinal.captainInclusion: DO NOT compact the captain. The user compacts the captain manually via the human /compact command. Only team members are compacted.
userDecisionsFinal.auditLocation: <workspace>/.mpd/team-compact/ - a separate namespace; never write .mpd/team (that state belongs to the agent-teams plugin).
userDecisionsFinal.deadCaptainTeams: Skip and record not-live. Architect measured that once a captain session is gone, workspaceRootsAll() no longer sees that team and its member Agents are not in-process, so it cannot be compacted anyway. Compact it after the team is resumed, if ever.
userDecisionsFinal.memberNotification: Silent, audit only - notifying a member would push context straight back in, the opposite of the point.
userDecisionsFinal.visibility: Also ship a READ-ONLY tool (e.g. mpd_team_compact_status) so the audit is inspectable from the agent surface. A Web-panel surface is explicitly a later slot, not this wave.

gateRetune.decision: Lower the thresholds AND widen the CJK vocabulary, calibrated on real prompts, then re-measure.
gateRetune.input: t37 measured 0/20 triggers on real prompts and caught a genuinely complex session-start request producing ZERO signals (1 B verb against a threshold of 4; 1 C2 verb against a threshold of 3). The observed cost is under-triggering, not over-triggering.
gateRetune.separateWorkItem: This is NOT part of the compaction plugin. It is a behaviour change and needs its own contract, mount proof and two-sided gate evidence.
gateRetune.coverageRequirement: The t39 verification's F2 finding stands: the 20-prompt set contained 0 Latin-only prompts, so the English trigger rate is undefined (n=0). Any recalibration set MUST cover English prompts explicitly or the bilingual claim is unsupported.

openFeasibilityQuestions: How does a sibling plugin learn that EVERY task of a team reached a terminal state - is there an event/service to subscribe to, or must it observe the team record on disk?
How does it map a team record's members to live Agent objects (does the record carry session/agent ids)?
What is the correct 'all members idle' barrier, and what happens to a member that becomes busy again mid-pass?
Is driving runMaintenance/compactNow on a continuable subagent session from a sibling plugin legitimate, or does it need the owning session's cooperation?

Does the compaction plane need to be composed in the plugin's own row context, and does the plugin need `compaction` in inject (a declared-but-unregistered service makes the loader entry pending and can fail the whole tree).

hardConstraints.singleWriterPlugin: packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin/** stays untouched by this feature (user chose a separate package).
hardConstraints.singleSkillsWriter: Any QA case under skills/** needs the corpus VENDOR_LOCK treeSha re-pinned in the SAME commit; serialize to exactly one skills writer.
hardConstraints.adapterRule: New mpd plugins reach harness seams through mpd-dsh-adapter (packages/mpd-dsh-adapter-plugin) - the one file allowed to touch ctx.tools/ctx.subagents/ctx.skills/ctx.agentPresets. The agent-teams plugin is the documented exception; a NEW plugin is not.
hardConstraints.bootProof: A new row must be proven by an isolated DSH_HOME boot that MOUNTS it with registration instrumentation; --dump-config proves composition only.
hardConstraints.noneRemoval: Compaction is destructive, so the feature must never fire inside a team that still has non-terminal tasks.
